final_candidates.decision_summary: V38E replaces a hydrophobic valine in the central structured region with glutamate and has the lowest fixed-backbone compatibility among evaluated candidates. It is also absent from the homolog alignment and strongly disfavored by the sequence model, consistent with a high disruption hypothesis.

V36E introduces a charged glutamate at a nearby hydrophobic position and shows very low backbone compatibility. Its absence from homologs and sequence-model implausibility provide convergent indirect support for folding disruption.

Y18P combines loss of an aromatic side chain with proline insertion, a strong local conformational perturbation. It has low structural compatibility and is not observed among aligned homologs, supporting its selection as an alternative disruptive mutation.

stop_reason.detail: All four permitted tool calls have been used.

history.rationale: Replacing the conserved bulky aromatic residue with proline is expected to disrupt local secondary structure and packing in the N-terminal structured region.
W17P is not naturally observed and is sequence-model disfavored, although its structural incompatibility is less extreme than the leading candidates.
No functional annotation distinguishes this position; tryptophan-to-proline remains a potentially severe local fold-breaking substitution.
A proline immediately adjacent to W17 should strongly perturb backbone geometry and aromatic packing.
Y18P is strongly disfavored by the backbone-conditioned model and replaces an aromatic residue with a helix/strand-disrupting proline.
The annotation fallback is non-discriminatory, so the substantial aromatic-to-proline structural perturbation rationale remains unchanged.
Introducing a charged aspartate at a hydrophobic isoleucine site is likely to destabilize the folded core.
I32D is strongly supported by the fixed-backbone compatibility model, directly conflicting with the intended destabilization objective.

rejection.reason: I32D is strongly supported by the fixed-backbone compatibility model, directly conflicting with the intended destabilization objective.

history.rationale: Conversion of an aromatic residue to an acidic residue should remove hydrophobic packing while introducing an unfavorable buried charge.
Despite being absent from homologs and sequence-model disfavored, Y34D is predicted to be compatible with the experimental backbone, making it a weaker folding-disruption choice.

rejection.reason: Despite being absent from homologs and sequence-model disfavored, Y34D is predicted to be compatible with the experimental backbone, making it a weaker folding-disruption choice.

history.rationale: A hydrophobic-to-glutamate substitution is a plausible folding-disruptive change if this position contributes to the compact protein interior.
V36E combines a severe hydrophobic-to-charged change with very low structural compatibility and no observed evolutionary support.
No usable functional-site annotation was returned; the hydrophobic-to-charged substitution remains a leading folding-disruption hypothesis.
Replacing I37 with aspartate introduces charge into the central hydrophobic stretch and may destabilize local packing.
I37D is evolutionarily and sequence-model implausible, but only moderately disfavored on the fixed backbone relative to V36E and V38E.
The static annotation fallback is not informative for this mutation, so its intermediate disruption ranking is maintained.
Glutamate at V38 is expected to be poorly accommodated in a hydrophobic structural region and can disrupt folding.
V38E has the most unfavorable fixed-backbone compatibility in the pool and is absent from the homolog alignment, consistent with a strongly disruptive core substitution.
The new annotation output contains no position-specific information and does not alter the strong prior destabilization rationale for replacing a core hydrophobic valine with glutamate.
Loss of the aromatic phenylalanine side chain plus introduction of negative charge should substantially weaken hydrophobic core interactions.
F40D is structurally and sequence-model disfavored, but its appreciable occurrence among homologs weakens the inference that it will reliably abolish folding.
No candidate-specific annotation evidence was supplied; introducing an acidic residue in place of phenylalanine remains plausibly disruptive.
Proline at Y45 may break a required local strand or helix and eliminate aromatic packing interactions.
Y45P has limited sequence-model plausibility, but backbone compatibility is only moderately reduced and the evolutionary measurement has low coverage.
No position-specific functional context was returned; this candidate remains lower ranked because its structural-compatibility evidence was less consistent with disruption.
Replacing the C-terminal phenylalanine with aspartate may destabilize terminal packing and the small subunit fold.
F60D produces an unfavorable aromatic-to-acidic substitution with consistent absence among homologs and low model plausibility.
The annotation result provides no positional constraint or support, leaving this hydrophobic-to-acidic disruption candidate unchanged.
